title: Create And Apply A Patch
background:
A practical starting point in *JsonPatch.Net* is to build a patch with operation factories and apply it to a document. This keeps the workflow concrete: define the transformation, then execute it to produce updated JSON.

This lesson focuses on creating a small patch in code and applying it to the provided input document. The objective is to produce the modified document as output.
instructions: Build a patch that replaces `/status` with `published`, apply it to `document`, and return the modified document.

title: Use PatchResult For Errors
background:
A key integration detail in *JsonPatch.Net* is that apply failures are reported through `PatchResult` rather than by defaulting to exception-driven flow. This gives you a predictable branch point for application logic and lets you return user-friendly messages without wrapping every apply call in broad catch blocks.

This lesson focuses on observing `PatchResult.Error` and `PatchResult.IsSuccess` after `Apply`. You will return a small status object that reports whether the operation succeeded and includes an error message only when the patch could not be applied.
instructions: Call `patch.Apply(document)` to get a `patchResult`. The scaffold will report `applied` or `failed` in `{ status, error }`.

title: Apply To Typed Model With Options
background:
*JsonPatch.Net* also supports patching typed .NET models through extension overloads. In that workflow, serializer configuration matters because patch paths are resolved against the serialized property names produced by your `JsonSerializerOptions`.

This lesson uses the typed apply overload that accepts `JsonSerializerOptions`. You will apply a patch to a deserialized model with camel-case naming and observe the updated model.
instructions: Apply the patch to the typed `Person` model by calling `patch.Apply(person, options)` and assigning the result back to `person`. The scaffold returns the updated model.

title: Create Patch From JsonNode
background:
*JsonPatch.Net* can generate patch documents by diffing start and target JSON values. This is useful when your application computes desired state and wants a compact patch payload to store, transmit, or apply later.

This lesson focuses on the `CreatePatch` extension for `JsonNode` values. You will generate the patch from two inputs and return the serialized patch document to inspect which operations the library produced.
instructions: Generate a patch from `start` to `target` using the `CreatePatch` extension on `JsonNode`. The scaffold returns the serialized patch.

title: Create Patch From Typed Models
background:
Patch generation is also available for typed object graphs through generic extension overloads. This lets your application work in domain types first, then produce patch documents from model-to-model differences without manual operation construction.

In this lesson, you will use the typed `CreatePatch<T>` overload with serializer options. The focus is selecting the typed diff-generation API and returning the generated patch document for inspection.
instructions: Generate a patch between typed `Person` values using `CreatePatch<T>` with serializer options. The scaffold returns the serialized patch.
